subject: Tidewell DPA: no-model-improvement opt-out + export/safeguards
messages:
From: Alex Browne <abrowne@tidewell.health>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tidewell Procurement <procurement@tidewell.health>, Priya Nambiar <priya.nambiar@tidewell.health>
Date: Sat, 28 Apr 2028 09:07:00 -0400
Subject: Redwood DPA follow-up — need confirmation on no-model-improve and data exports

Stephanie — thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and legal ran through the DPA draft and we have a couple of tight asks before we can proceed to signature. Short list below: 

1) A firm "no model improvement / no training" commitment for Tidewell customer data (including prompts and generated responses). We need language that prevents use for model updates and a description of the controls you use to ensure that.
2) A list of subprocessors that will see customer content in any form (including logging, QA, telemetry).
3) Data transfer/export safeguards — Tidewell requires onshore routing for PHI-adjacent payloads and clarity on any cross-border transfers (SCCs or equivalent).

Attached is our redlines file (Tidewell_DPA_Draft_v3.docx). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an attestation letter and a short operational note on how the no-train commitment is enforced (e.g., storage TTLs, KV caching behavior, and S3/SFTP export lanes)? Also, do you support KMS key control per-customer for managed instances?

If this is easier, loop in privacy/legal on your side and we can schedule a 30 min call next week.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Director, Vendor Risk
Tidewell Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Browne <abrowne@tidewell.health>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA follow-up — need confirmation on no-model-improve and data exports

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. We're aligned on wanting tight controls for healthcare customers. Quick answers up front, then I’ll loop in David and Kimberly with evidence and proposed contract language: 

• No-model-improvement: Redwood will not use customer-provided content (prompts, prompt-response pairs, attachments) to improve or fine-tune any model used to serve Tidewell. We can commit to a no-training clause in the DPA and provide an attestation letter.
• Subprocessors: I’ve attached the current subprocessor CSV (redwood-subprocessors-2028-04.csv). We will provide the formal attestation listing versions and access tiers.
• Data transfer/onshore routing: For Tidewell we can pin routes to US-only regions and offer an SFTP export lane that stays in US regions. If SCCs are required for any EU transfer in the future, we can add the standard EU transfer clauses — but for this deal everything will be routed to US-only endpoints per your ask.

Action items for us: David will produce a short ops note describing how we prevent training (config flags, ingestion paths excluded from telemetry, TTLs), and Kimberly will propose lock-tight contract language and an attestation template you can sign.

Would you prefer the attestation as a separate signed letter or as an addendum clause in the DPA? If you can share Tidewell's preferred form (a short template is fine) we’ll mirror it.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Enterprise/API
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Browne <abrowne@tidewell.health>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA follow-up — need confirmation on no-model-improve and data exports

Alex / Stephanie — forwarding the operational detail Alex requested. Kevin from Infra would normally produce the deep tech note but I can summarize the controls that enforce the "no model improvement" commitment for Tidewell: 

1) Logical segmentation: Requests from Tidewell accounts are tagged with a tenant ID at ingress. Those tags determine downstream routing and telemetry pipelines. By default, we maintain two downstream paths: (a) "serving" which retains ephemeral KV cache and request metadata for short-term inference correctness (TTL configurable), and (b) "telemetry" which receives sanitized anonymized metrics only.

2) Training blackout: We have a platform-level flag (customer_learning_opt_in=false) that prevents any flow of customer content into training datasets or model tuning pipelines. This flag is applied at tenant ID and is audited monthly. For Tidewell it will be set to false and locked by legal/contract.

3) Retention & TTLs: Ephemeral request context (including KV cache and prefix cache) is kept for up to 48 hours by default; logs that include partial prompt/response fingerprints are retained for 30 days and are hashed/available only to SRE for debugging. We can shorten TTLs per contract and offer an ephemeral-only mode (no persistent logs beyond 7 days).

4) Subprocessor access: The included CSV shows third parties used for monitoring, S3 storage, and hosting control plane. Access tiers are limited: only the hosting provider's control plane sees encrypted blobs; application logs are redacted. We will provide a signed subprocessor attestation that lists people/groups with access and the purpose.

5) Key management & onshore routing: For Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys (Bring Your Own Key) and can configure all storage/export paths to US regions. For Hosted API we can offer account-level KMS wrapping and regional routing; we will document the exact lane that Tidewell traffic traverses.

6) Export lanes: We support SFTP push to a Tidewell-managed SFTP endpoint in your VPC or a managed S3 bucket inside a US-only account. All exports can be restricted to the US with audit logs.

If Tidewell would like a signed attestation, Stephanie — can Kimberly confirm the legal phrasing? Alex — curious whether you want the attestation to mention monthly audits and an incident escalation contact.

-David
David Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Browne <abrowne@tidewell.health>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Apr 2028 14:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA follow-up — need confirmation on no-model-improve and data exports

Alex — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks. Proposed next steps and contract language snippet below. I kept it short so your legal/procurement can drop it into your redlines if it looks good: 

PROPOSED CLAUSE (short form):
"Supplier (Redwood Inference) shall not use Customer Data including prompts, prompt-response pairs, uploaded attachments, or derived outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning model or dataset used by Supplier or its subprocessors, now or in the future, unless Supplier obtains Customer's prior written consent. Supplier shall maintain and enforce technical controls to prevent Customer Data being ingested into any training or model development pipelines and shall provide an attestation of such controls upon Customer's request."

ADDITIONAL OPS ATTACHMENT (to attach to DPA):
• Monthly subprocessor attestation (signed)
• Onshore routing statement (US-only)
• Operational note: customer_learning_opt_in flag status and TTLs
• Audit schedule and incident escalation contact

We can produce the attestation as a PDF signed by Redwood Legal. If Tidewell has a preferred signature block / acceptance method we can follow that (addendum vs separate attestation).

If you're OK with the language above, I’ll insert it into the DPA redline (Tidewell_DPA_Draft_v3.docx) and return a version for signature. If you prefer a call, we’re available Mon/Tue next week; I’d suggest 30 minutes with procurement + legal + David to confirm ops detail.

-Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
